A streetlamp flickered, its pale light casting jittery shadows that danced along the damp cobblestones. Elena pulled her coat tighter around her, a futile attempt to shield herself from the chill that gnawed at her bones. Her breath formed little clouds in the air, dissipating almost immediately as she stepped deeper into the shadows, her boots crunching softly on the scattered debris.

She paused, leaning against the cool brick wall, her heart racing as she listened for the telltale sound of footsteps. The world felt suspended in those moments, the usual hum of the city reduced to a distant echo. She could hear the faint murmur of waves crashing against the shore, a steady rhythm that seemed to pulse in time with her anxious heartbeat. Had she imagined the rustling? Just the wind, surely. Yet, the prickle of unease crawled up her spine, urging her to move.

“Elena?” The voice sliced through the silence, low and cautious. It was Marco, stepping out from the recesses of the shadows, his face half-illuminated by the waning light.
